text.p: Here is how major stock markets outside the United States ended Tuesday.

LONDON - A two-day British stock rally ran out of steam Tuesday as a weak Wall Street and continued worries about possible interest rate hikes pushed prices marginally lower. The FTSE 100 index of leading shares closed 2.4 points down to 4,269.3.

FRANKFURT - German stocks were off the day's highs and below the high levels seen late Monday in afternoon trading, as the market took a pause for breath after surging 3 percent Monday. The DAX index ended up 16.88 points at 3,329.76. In after-market trade, the index fell 14.64 to 3,328.13.

PARIS - French stocks, drawing support from dollar strength, limped to a higher close. But traders said the market lacked volume to make a convincing advance. The blue-chip CAC-40 index closed up 6.69 points, or 0.26 percent, at 2,579.

ZURICH - Swiss stocks recovered from early weakness to end little changed in quiet trade after Monday's 2.6 percent jump. Dealers said insecurity about further developments on Wall Street kept a lid on stocks. They said directionless trade may last until Friday, when U.S. economic data are due. The all-share Swiss Performance Index (SPI) closed 4.19 points lower at 2,898.96.

TOKYO - Tokyo stocks ended Tuesday's session with sharp gains after stocks rallied, inspired by the yen's weakness against the dollar, brokers said. But they said sectors burdened by bad loans were still weak. The 225-share Nikkei average rose 306.03 points, or 1.73 percent, to end at 18,021.70.

HONG KONG - Hong Kong stocks closed higher Tuesday, helped by interest in HSBC Holdings, while trading volumes appeared to be slowly increasing. The Hang Seng Index finished up 110.73 points, or 0.90 percent, at 12,398.57.

SYDNEY - A sleepy Australian stock market ended a dull day barely higher Tuesday with hesitant investors reluctant to commit funds to a drifting market. The All Ordinaries index added 2.9 points to close at 2,368.9.

JOHANNESBURG - South African industrial stocks ended near the day's weakest levels after a slow drift down on profit-taking and futures arbitrage activity. Gold stocks stayed firm as the price of bullion bounced around the $349 level. The industrial index ended down 40.9 points at 8,244.7. The gold index added 9.8 points to 1,327.8 and the overall index fell 30.6 to 7,044.1.
